title: Kitchen and Backyard Gardening
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Lay out a small kitchen garden near the school kitchen: a keyhole bed or a few raised or sunken beds with vegetables, herbs (dhania, mint) and spices. Each group cares for one bed.

skills.key_step: The child explains the role of a kitchen and backyard garden: fresh, healthy food close at hand, a balanced diet, money saved, extra to sell, use of small spaces and household water, and space for herbs and spices.

floor.prerequisite: Knows vertical and horizontal innovative gardens.
floor.question: Name an innovative garden.

board.do: Ask how much is spent in a month.

misconceptions.ask: Where is a kitchen garden kept?
misconceptions.repair: Show a keyhole garden two steps from a kitchen door.

misconceptions.ask: Which crop suits a kitchen garden?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what the cook needs every day: greens, onions, tomatoes, herbs.

misconceptions.ask: How does a kitchen garden help a family?
misconceptions.repair: Count the shillings spent on sukuma wiki in a month against a packet of seed.

listen_for: One crop in a large amount
misconceptions.ask: What is grown in a kitchen garden?
misconceptions.repair: Show a kitchen garden plan with many small patches.

checks.question: Give two roles of a kitchen garden.
checks.answer: any two of fresh food, saving money, balanced diet, income

checks.question: Where is a kitchen garden usually placed?

skills.key_step: The child says how a kitchen or backyard garden is established: sunny site near the house and water, fence, prepare beds with manure (or a keyhole bed), plant a mix of crops in staggered small amounts, water, weed, harvest often.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the role of a kitchen garden.
floor.question: Why have a kitchen garden?

steps: Choose a sunny site near the house.
Fence it; prepare beds with manure.
Plant a mix in small amounts every few weeks.

board.do: Draw a calendar with one big planting in March.
Ask when there will be no vegetables.
Draw small plantings every three weeks.

misconceptions.ask: How can a kitchen garden give vegetables all the time?
misconceptions.repair: Draw a harvest calendar for one planting and for staggered plantings.

listen_for: Far from the house in the shade
misconceptions.ask: Where is a kitchen garden best placed?
misconceptions.repair: Ask how often the cook goes to pick greens, and how water is carried.
Show a bed scratched by chickens.

listen_for: None, herbs come only from shops
misconceptions.ask: Which herb can be grown in a kitchen garden?
misconceptions.repair: Grow dhania in a tin in class.

checks.question: Why plant small amounts every few weeks?
